subject: Invoice submission: portal idempotency, subject token, and email fallback
messages:
From: Kenji Saito <kenji@brightwave.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice submission: portal idempotency, subject token, and email fallback

Hi Olga / Vanessa / Ben,

Thanks for the onboarding checklist you sent last week. We're doing a pilot of your portal integration this month and ran into two things we want to iron out before go-live:

1) Duplicate prevention / idempotency: our ERP can retry HTTP uploads when it sees transient errors. We need to know what the portal considers a duplicate (invoice number + vendor? subject token?) and how the portal surfaces a duplicate (204 / 409 / specific header).

2) Email fallback subject token: some of our smaller processing partners will send invoices by email when the portal is unavailable. We want a small, consistent subject convention so the email parser can extract vendor, PO match fields, and an idempotency token. Can you share the recommended subject format and an example of the ack the portal would send back?

I've attached a sample invoice (brightwave_sample_invoice_v2.xlsx) and a short CSV with multi-PO line examples.

Also: in multi-PO invoices, we sometimes put multiple PO numbers on one line — how strict is Redwood on line-level PO mapping vs. header-level PO mapping?

Appreciate any concrete examples.

Thanks,
Kenji Saito
AP Lead, BrightWave Logistics
kenji@brightwave.com
+1 415-555-0182

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission: portal idempotency, subject token, and email fallback

Hi Kenji — thanks for the sample and the clear list. Short answers up front, then a proposal.

- Duplicate detection: portal uses invoice_number + vendor_id + total_amount as the primary idempotency key. If an identical key is received within 72 hours, the portal returns 409 with a JSON body referencing the original document id and an X-RWI-Ack header (example below). Retries that change amount or invoice_number are treated as new.

- Email subject token: we recommend a compact subject token to enable robust parsing. Proposed format: RWI:{vendor_short}:{invoice#}:{idempotency_token}  (example: RWI:BRW:INV-20280314-452:b63f9c). The token can be any 8-12 hex chars generated by the sender; the portal will verify uniqueness and return it in the ack.

- Multi-PO behavior: default mapping is header-level PO matching. We support explicit line-level PO mappings when the invoice includes a PO-Mapping table (we accept a compact CSV blob in the invoice metadata or a standardized line item table). If you need line-level enforcement, we can flip that flag for your tenant.

Proposal:
1) For portal uploads: use invoice_number + vendor_id + idempotency_token in the metadata. Portal will return 201 for new, 409 for dup with header X-RWI-Ack: token=<token>;status=duplicate;orig_id=<id>.
2) For email fallback: require the subject token as above and include a short header in the email body: RWI-Token: <token> and RWI-PO-MAP: header|line (optional). We will run the parser to extract attachments, then post to the same ingestion pipeline, preserving the idempotency token.

I'm attaching a brief spec with examples: proposed_subject_token_spec.txt.

If this works, Ben can follow up with the portal response header example and the sample webhook ack payload.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Program Manager, Procurement Integrations
Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

Kenji / team — quick technical note on portal behavior and idempotency headers so your engineering team can map it: 

Example portal responses for duplicate uploads:
- HTTP 409
- Response body: {"status":"duplicate","original_id":"rwi-20280314-00012","reason":"matching invoice_number+vendor+amount"}
- Response headers: X-RWI-Ack: token=b63f9c;status=duplicate;orig_id=rwi-20280314-00012
- Retry guidance: if you change the content (amount, invoice_number), treat as new submission; if retrying due to timeout, resend same idempotency_token.

Email fallback parsing behavior:
- Parser scans subject for /^RWI:([A-Z0-9]{2,6}):([^:]+):([a-f0-9]{8,12})/
- It will look for an optional body header line: RWI-PO-MAP: header|line
- Attachments: first PDF/XLSX is treated as primary invoice; additional files marked as supporting docs.

We also expose a webhook ack (POST) that returns a flattened JSON ack including the token, ingestion_id, and canonical_status. Example: POST /hooks/ack -> {"token":"b63f9c","ingestion_id":"rwi-20280315-2108","status":"received"}.

If BrightWave needs stricter line-level PO enforcement, we can enable that for your tenant and include a rejection reason in the ack.

On the PO mapping question: please send a short sample of the multi-PO layout you referenced (if different from the attached CSV), and we'll validate the mapping rules against our parser tonight.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Billing Integrations Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Olga / Ben / team — thanks, this is very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups so we can finalize our go-live checklist: 

1) Email fallback timing: if the portal ingestor is down and our partner emails the AP inbox, what is the expected SLA for the parser to pick it up and return an ack? We need this to set partner expectations (and our retry windows).
2) Final PO mapping: attached is a tiny CSV example of the multi-PO-per-line case (same as the original spreadsheet, second tab). If Redwood can do header-level mapping by default and optionally enforce line-level mapping when configured, that meets our needs. Please confirm the default will accept header-level mapping and not reject on ambiguous line entries.

If you confirm the above we'll draft an internal partner note with the subject token regex and retry guidance and schedule the pilot cutover next Tuesday.

Cheers,
Kenji
AP Lead, BrightWave Logistics
